remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Sold to Mrs. Arthur Schwab. Note: When I met Mrs. Schwab the night of the O'Keeffe opening at the Metropolitan Museum of Art she told me she still owned this painting." Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Exam. at Mrs. Schwab's apartment June 25, 1946. . . . Did not see back." Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Possibly No. 6 in 1928 exhibition. Rosalind Irvine." See cat. nos. 520, 521. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

credit_line: Bequest of Mrs. Arthur Schwab (Edna Bryner, class of 1907)
description: A bluish-gray river, seen from a high vantage point, runs through the center of the canvas. In the foreground, the bright white roofs of buildings are visible, while the background features tall structures with smokestacks emitting white steam.
imageCaption: Courtesy of Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
